title: Giant nonlinear Hall effect in a Pt/ferrimagnetic insulator bilayer under Zeeman-exchange frustration
authors: Takayuki Shiino, Matteo Fettizio, Weronika Janus, Can Onur Avci
abstract: Competing magnetic interactions can create metastable or unstable states and render magnetic systems highly susceptible to external perturbations. Here we show that Zeeman-exchange frustration in an Al-substituted terbium iron garnet with a compositional gradient across its thickness gives rise to a giant nonlinear Hall response in an adjacent Pt layer. Near magnetic compensation, a field-induced spin-flip transition is accompanied by unusually large higher-order odd harmonic voltages, with the third, fifth, and seventh harmonics reaching amplitudes comparable to that of the first harmonic. The field, temperature, and current dependences collectively identify Joule heating as the parametric drive of the harmonic response. Macrospin-chain simulations further show that current-induced thermal modulation periodically switches the interfacial Fe magnetization between exchange- and Zeeman-dominated states and reproduces the observed harmonic signals. These results demonstrate how frustration can convert a weak thermal perturbation into a large nonlinear electrical response, providing a route to nonlinear magnetotransport in compensated ferrimagnets.
summary: This work demonstrates that in ferrimagnetic insulators exhibiting Zeeman-exchange frustration, Joule heating can parametrically drive the magnetization through unstable spin-flip regimes. This process converts a weak thermal fluctuation into a giant nonlinear electrical signal characterized by large odd harmonic voltages, opening new avenues for controlling magnetotransport via thermal effects.
main_problem: The study investigates how Zeeman-exchange frustration can convert a weak thermal perturbation into a large nonlinear electrical response in magnetic heterostructures.
main_result: Large, higher-order odd harmonic voltages are generated when the system is driven through a spin-flip transition regime by Joule heating, demonstrating a novel route for nonlinear magnetotransport.
method: The research combines experimental measurements of harmonic Hall voltage with advanced macrospin-chain simulations incorporating thermal modulation effects.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an Al:TbIG/Pt bilayer exhibiting compositional gradients. The model uses a 1D chain of coupled spins governed by effective fields including exchange, anisotropy, and Zeeman terms.
key_observables: Odd-order harmonic Hall voltages ($V_{3\omega}^H, V_{5\omega}^H, V_{7\omega}^H$), spin-flip transitions, and the field/temperature dependence of these harmonics.
important_parameters: Zeeman-exchange frustration regime, magnetic compensation point, current density (driving Joule heating), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The nonlinear response is primarily driven by parametric modulation induced by Joule heating causing periodic switching between competing magnetic states, rather than just spin-orbit torque effects.
figures_summary: Figures show structural gradients via STEM/EELS; transport measurements reveal large odd harmonics confined to a specific field window when current density increases; simulations confirm these harmonics arise from thermal modulation driving magnetization switching across stability boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the problem of nonlinearity. It presents experimental evidence showing large odd harmonics, which are then theoretically explained by macrospin-chain simulations that explicitly model Joule heating as the parametric drive causing periodic magnetic state switching.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on non-equilibrium thermodynamics (Joule heating) driving a system through a critical point (frustration/compensation), leading to macroscopic nonlinear response, which is relevant for understanding driven quantum or classical many-body systems near phase transitions.
